cards.text: Psalm 105 opens like a hype man grabbing the mic. The singer is talking to the offspring of Abraham, the father of Israel's family line, and to the sons of Jacob, Abraham's grandson. His first words are give thanks to the LORD and call upon His name.

cards.question: The singer wants the LORD's deeds told, not kept quiet. Among whom should His deeds be made known?
The singer tells God's people to sing to the LORD and tell of only a few of His wonders.

cards.text: Glory in His holy name, he says, and let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice. That's not a chore list, friend, that's a PARTY invitation.

cards.question: The singer says to seek out the LORD and His strength. How often should they seek His face?

cards.text: Then comes a word this whole song keeps coming back to: remember.

cards.question: The singer tells God's people to remember. Remember what?
The singer says the LORD's judgments reach only as far as Israel.

cards.text: Now here's the flip. God's people are told to remember, but the singer says God remembers too.

cards.question: What does God remember forever?

cards.text: His covenant, forever, the word He ordained for a thousand generations. Me? I set the oven timer, walk three steps and forget there's a timer.

cards.question: The singer names who received the promise: the covenant God made with ___ and the oath He swore to ___.

cards.text: Isaac is Abraham's son, and God confirmed it to Isaac's son Jacob, also called Israel, as an everlasting covenant. Passed down three generations like a family heirloom, while I got passed down to a junk drawer.

cards.question: In that covenant, God promises to give them the land of ___ as the portion of their inheritance.

cards.text: But back then, they were few in number, few indeed, and strangers in the land. That's like getting handed the keys to a house nobody has built yet.

cards.question: Few in number and strangers in the land. What do they do?
As they wander, God lets other people push them around.
God even rebukes ___ on their behalf.

cards.text: KINGS, friend, crown on the head and an army out back, and God tells them, "Do not touch My anointed ones! Do no harm to My prophets!"
Then the song turns hard. God called down famine on the land and cut off all their supplies of food.

cards.question: God sends a man before them. Who is it?
Joseph goes ahead of them as an honored guest.

cards.text: Joseph, one of Jacob's sons, was sold as a slave, and they bruised his feet with shackles and put his neck in irons. I thought the junk drawer was rough, and the worst I ever got back there was snapped by a rubber band I shared that drawer with.

cards.question: How long does Joseph stay in irons?

answers.text: Until his brothers came for him

cards.text: And the word of the LORD proved him right. Joseph called it, and God backed him up.

cards.question: Joseph's father sends for him and gets him released.

cards.text: The king sent and released him, then made him master of his household, ruler over all his substance. Three verses ago his neck was in irons, and now he's running the king's whole house!

cards.question: Joseph gets to instruct the king's princes as he pleases and teach the king's elders ___.

cards.text: Joseph's in charge. Now the rest of the family makes a move.

cards.question: Jacob's family moves to ___.

cards.text: Israel entered Egypt, and Jacob dwelt in the land of Ham. The family that wandered from kingdom to kingdom finally has an address.

cards.question: What does the LORD do for His people in Egypt?
The singer says Israel grows more numerous than their foes.

cards.text: Remember few in number, few indeed? Not anymore, that's a group chat that started with three people and now nobody can find their own messages.

cards.question: Then something happens to the hearts of Israel's foes. What?

answers.text: God turned them to hate His people
God softened them toward His people
God made them forget His people

cards.text: Now they conspire against His servants. Big family, hostile neighbors, and things in Egypt are about to get loud.
Things are tense in Egypt, so God sends someone. Actually, two someones.

cards.question: Who does God send to His people in Egypt?

cards.text: Moses, Israel's leader, and Aaron, his brother (Exodus 4:14), whom God had chosen. They perform His miraculous signs and wonders in the land of Ham.

cards.question: God sends darkness on Egypt, and Egypt obeys His words.
Next, God turns Egypt's waters to ___.

cards.text: Their fish die, and then their land teems with frogs, even in their ROYAL chambers. Guards at the door, gold on the walls, and a frog sitting on the king's pillow.
God speaks, and gnats swarm throughout their country. Then He gives them hail for rain, with lightning throughout their land.

cards.question: God strikes Egypt's vines and fig trees.

cards.text: He speaks, and locusts come, young locusts without number, devouring every plant in their land. WITHOUT NUMBER, friend, that's not a swarm, that's a stadium letting out.

cards.question: Then comes the final blow in this song. What does God strike?

answers.text: All the firstborn in their land
All the cattle in their fields
All the palaces of their king

cards.question: God brings Israel out of Egypt empty-handed.

cards.text: He brought them out with silver and gold, none among His tribes stumbled, and Egypt was glad when they departed, for the dread of Israel had fallen on them. Egypt didn't just wave goodbye, friend, Egypt HELD THE DOOR.

cards.question: On the way, God gives His people a covering and a light for the night. What are they?

cards.text: They asked, and He brought quail and satisfied them with the bread of heaven. Not a little snack, friend, SATISFIED.

cards.question: Out in the desert, God opens a ___ and water gushes out like a river.
The singer stops and tells why God did all this. Why?

answers.text: He remembered His promise to Abraham

cards.text: There's that remembering again, His holy promise to Abraham His servant. And He brought forth His people with rejoicing, His chosen with shouts of joy.

cards.question: God gives His people the lands of the nations, and they inherit the fruit of others' labor. What is it all for?

answers.text: So they would keep His laws
So they would build an army
So they would rule over Egypt

cards.text: Hallelujah! God remembers His promise for a thousand generations, and I throw myself a party when I remember I set a timer.

findings.problem: The card states facts from outside the passage with no reference: Abraham is 'the father of Israel's family line' and Jacob is 'Abraham's grandson.' Stop 3 card 3 gives a reference for Aaron, so the walkthrough handles this inconsistently.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: 'In that covenant, God promises to give them' points back to a card the baker can no longer see. 'That covenant' and 'them' are not identified in the question.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The comparison does not match the action. In v12 the land exists and they are strangers living in it. 'Keys to a house nobody has built yet' suggests the promised land doesn't exist yet. The joke also blurs what the text says.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new drawer incident: Papa Dorin being snapped by a rubber band. Made-up moments are allowed only around his bakery. The backstory itself must not be added to.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: 'Things are tense in Egypt, so God sends someone' adds a reason for sending Moses and Aaron. The text does not give one. v26 simply follows v25.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: 'Next, God turns Egypt's waters to blood' adds an order the psalm doesn't give. Exodus shows the water turned to blood before the darkness (Exodus 7:20; 10:22), so 'next' implies something the text shows is wrong.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The card carries three beats in one long first sentence: the silver and gold, none of the tribes stumbling, and Egypt being glad because of dread. That is more than two things happening.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: Several story cards call back to an earlier verse but cite only the current verse. Stop 3 card 19 cites Psalm 105:45 but restates v8 ('a thousand generations'). Stop 2 card 12 cites v23 but uses v13 ('wandered from kingdom to kingdom'). Stop 2 card 15 cites v24 but quotes v12 ('few in number, few indeed'). Applied literally, the citation rule gives wide ranges like Psalm 105:8-45.
findings.question: When a story card calls back to wording from an earlier verse in the same passage, should the citation widen to cover it, list both verses, or cite only the verse the card moves forward on?
